Milo —

Quick check: I still can’t see any Sundrift relaunch notes in the trades; assuming uptime hardening is still in flight. Here’s the one‑pager you can drop straight into sprint.

Objective + signal
- Optimise to one conversion event (first purchase or subscription start). Dedupe pixel/server events; reconcile to orders daily in week one so GEM learns the right lesson.

Concept set (2–3 total)
- Build around distinct occasions/use‑cases (emotion > ingredient). One promise per concept, stated in frame 1 and line 1. Keep concepts separable in naming and UTMs.

Asset matrix per concept (minimum viable)
- Video (9:16): two core hooks — (a) pack + promise in 0–3s; (b) demo/pour/mix. Cut each to 4:5 and 1:1.  
- Static (4:5): (a) plain offer (pack + price/launch deal), (b) proof‑led (quote/rating + pack).  
- Story/Reel sequence: 3–4 frames — hook, benefit, offer, CTA.  
- Creator variant: same beats, different face.  
- Copy: one price‑forward, one payoff‑forward. UTM by concept → matched page.

Campaign design for GEM
- One CBO conversion campaign, open placements. 2–3 ad sets total (geo/age/safety guardrails only). Don’t split by placement; let the model allocate surface + creative.
- Broad targeting; creative variety drives learning, not micro audience splits.

Pacing for ~£120k/mo
- Prospecting majority; hold a modest launch‑day surge; keep remarketing lean until the pool builds (first 7–10 days), then scale if CPA holds.

Cadence + decision rules
- Add 1–2 fresh variants weekly so nothing gets stale. If a variant declines for three consecutive reads, rotate it out; promote winners at the concept level (not just the asset).

Ad → page mapping (build order)
- Ship three pages matched to the three promises:  
  1) Plain offer (hero pack + price/offer, singular CTA) — first live.  
  2) Proof‑heavy (reviews/nutrition/comparison/FAQs) — for risk/novelty.  
  3) Chooser (3‑step) — for bundles/gifting.  
- Call a winner per concept after 500–1,000 qualified sessions or 3 days (whichever first), then route spend accordingly.

Readiness gates (day‑zero)
- Multi‑region uptime monitoring + CDN/WAF; keep a lightweight fallback page on a separate host.  
- If main app isn’t rock‑solid for 48h, point ads to the fallback; switch over once stable.

Reporting + naming
- Daily cut by concept → surface → asset; avoid audience‑level noise.  
- Naming example: sd_jan_c1_reset_v2_45 (brand_month_concept_variant_aspect).

Delivery checklist (for 3 concepts)
- 6 core videos (9:16) + 12 cuts (4:5/1:1), 6 statics, 3 Story sequences, 3 creator variants, 6 copy blocks (2 per concept). Total: 30+ deployable units with clear IDs.

If helpful, I can follow with a one‑pager fallback landing wireframe and the ad‑to‑offer mapping rubric.
